key_insight: An LLM-assisted registry analysis found that changes to trial primary outcomes and arms/interventions were associated with higher odds of primary endpoint positivity.
clinical_relevance: This research-integrity tool could help reviewers assess trial-reporting transparency; it does not evaluate cancer drugs or guide treatment.
method: Extract randomized trial records and version histories from ClinicalTrials.gov.
Detect registry changes using deterministic text analysis and LLM-assisted classification.
Assess associations between registry changes, their timing, and primary endpoint positivity.
evidence_signal: Primary outcome changes were associated with positivity (OR 1.91; 95% CI 1.48–2.47), as were arms/intervention changes (OR 2.10; 95% CI 1.62–2.73); associations were weaker for changes occurring exclusively before primary completion.
watch_item: These associations do not establish causation or misconduct, and the abstract does not report LLM classification accuracy.
paper_title: An LLM-assisted Pipeline for Identifying ClinicalTrials.gov Registry Changes and Their Association with Primary Endpoint Positivity
